Social Sciences [SSCI]
Music Ensembles: 7 ensemble credits required on the student’s major instrument with at least 4 credits from MUS 429, 430, 431, 432, 434, 435 (guitar ensemble only), 436, 437, 438, or 441. 3 credits taken from ensemble courses designated as ARTS fulfill the [ARTS] UCORE requirement.

Each student desiring to pursue a music major at WSU must have an audition with the studio teacher of the major instrument or voice of intended study, and in the case of multiple teachers in the studio, with the area coordinator. Faculty and students are encouraged to set up an audition before the semester, use the first lesson as an audition, or use the ensemble placement audition as the audition. 

To be admitted as a major pursuing any degree in music, students must meet the following criteria:

1. Successfully audition into 300-level lessons on their major instrument or voice.
2. Enroll in MUS 251 and 252 or be approved to receive transfer credit by the Music Theory Area Coordinator.

This major offers professional preparation in music with specialization in the music industry. The curriculum is designed to prepare students in entrepreneurship, artist management, music marketing and promotion, sound production, music publishing, booking and tour management, copyright, contract and negotiation, concert staging work, music technology, and retail operations.

Requirements include: second-year assessment; piano proficiency exam; achieve a cumulative 2.5 GPA and a grade of C or better in all music classes; a senior half recital. Students are expected to perform in an ensemble on their major instrument during each semester of applied lessons. Additional ensemble requirements are clarified below. Any exceptions must be arranged with the instructor of the applied lessons.

Only 9 credits of MUS courses can be used to fulfill UCORE requirements.
